chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon them both) who said:
"When the young child is capable of fasting for three consecutive days, then fasting the month of Ramadan becomes obligatory upon him."
ai.seo_question: At what age or stage of ability does fasting become obligatory for children in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the transition from voluntary practice to obligatory fasting (wujub) for children, emphasizing physical capacity (itaqa) as the key criterion. It reflects the scholarly principle that while fasting is not strictly mandatory until puberty, the gradual training period serves as a preparatory phase where consistent ability triggers the binding nature of the duty. This ruling underscores the practical application of readiness over mere age in determining religious accountability.
